title: C1107 — Output shaft speed (OSS) sensor connector
introduction:
I read this reference like a contact list for the output shaft speed (OSS) sensor: identify the connector, match the drawing’s cavity labels to the circuit rows, then use the parts table for catalog lookup. The Function column explains each connection’s assigned job; it cannot tell us whether that connection is working. An address book is useful, but it cannot answer the phone for you.

This guide covers identification and reading the reference. It does not establish access, the physical viewing direction, electrical test conditions or repair methods. The gauge convention and the Size and Used codes are undefined here, so I leave them uninterpreted.

edits.why: I use the vertically arranged cavity labels and the projecting housing details on the left as landmarks within this drawing. Match each label to the Cavity column below; the illustration’s position on the page does not establish which side of the physical connector to view.

Read across a single Cavity row to keep its Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function and Terminal Part Number together. The function descriptions distinguish the buffered supply, sensor connection and signal-return roles. Those labels identify circuit purposes; they are not measurements or proof of a healthy circuit.

I keep Service Part and Engineering Shell distinct when reading the catalog record: the service identifier and housing identifier serve different lookup purposes. The Image entry names a catalog illustration. The pigtail and pin-assignment gauge entries belong to their respective records and do not establish a wire substitution or splice method.
